summary: Interprets receipt f87365ea88ba4a48a610ba8f380419b0, which replaces the synthetic delay in the heartbeat term race with a real file write plus fsync on every current-term update. 89 of 200 attempts inverted, with 402 term writes, a mean write of 1.993 ms and a maximum of 16.2 ms. That shows the exposure under genuine filesystem latency of the order a containerised deployment has, not only under an injected sleep, and the measured mean falls inside the range where the earlier delay sweep showed the rate saturated, so the sweep's curve and this real-latency run agree on the mechanism. The account keeps its violated conclusion and asserted defect, extends the rationale with the receipt's parsed indices, and replaces the counterevidence entry that said the delay was only a sleep before an in-memory write with one recording the real-latency result while noting that the latency is still this container's filesystem rather than any particular deployment's storage stack. Knowledge entries 830b0f3ff5a14266b056ad4a6d0c877b-knowledge-0 and -1 carry the new receipt's executions for unchanged statements, and joint_history notes that it comes from a further experiment identifier keeping the attempt body, request shapes and inversion criterion and changing only the source of the latency. The submission validates with zero schema errors and requests no execution.
